question: What is the primary goal of food safety in primary health care?

options.D: Eliminating the need for food markets

explanation: Primary health care focuses on disease prevention and health promotion, making the prevention of foodborne illness a core objective. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h1)

question: Which group suffers most severely from unsafe food in local communities?
explanation: Young children have developing immune systems and lower body reserves, making them highly vulnerable to dehydration from foodborne infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h1)

question: What action prevents harmful bacteria from transferring between raw meat and ready-to-eat food?
explanation: Physical separation using different cutting boards and storage areas stops microbes from moving from raw ingredients to cooked meals. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h2)

question: Why must perishable cooked foods be refrigerated promptly after preparation?

options.A: To improve the overall taste and texture of the meal
options.B: To slow down the rapid multiplication of bacteria
options.C: To prevent the loss of essential vitamins and minerals
options.D: To remove chemical preservatives added during cooking

explanation: Bacteria multiply rapidly in the temperature danger zone, so refrigeration slows their growth to keep food safe. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h2)

question: Which pathogen is commonly transmitted through undercooked poultry and raw eggs?
explanation: Salmonella bacteria naturally colonize the intestinal tracts of poultry and frequently contaminate eggs and meat. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h3)

question: A patient presents with severe watery diarrhea after drinking unverified borehole water during an outbreak. What organism is suspected?
explanation: Vibrio cholerae causes acute watery diarrhea and is primarily spread through water supplies contaminated with faecal matter. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h3)

question: What is the single most effective barrier against microbial transfer during food preparation?

options.A: Rinsing utensils in cold river water
options.B: Sprinkling antiseptic powder on raw food
options.C: Wearing thick leather gloves while cooking
options.D: Proper handwashing with soap and clean water

explanation: Handwashing removes transient pathogens picked up from surfaces, animals, and body parts before they touch edible items. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h4)

question: Why should a food handler with an infected skin boil be restricted from cooking duties?

options.A: They will absorb toxins directly from the cooking oil
options.B: They can contaminate food with Staphylococcus bacteria from the lesion
options.C: They will easily burn themselves due to reduced skin sensitivity
options.D: They cannot lift heavy pots with an injured hand

explanation: Skin boils are a common reservoir for Staphylococcus aureus, which produces heat-stable toxins that cause severe food poisoning. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h4)

question: What is a reliable method to make untreated borehole water safe for food preparation?

options.C: Adding small amounts of cooking oil
options.D: Straining the water through a cloth

explanation: Heat from boiling effectively kills harmful bacteria, viruses, and parasites present in untreated water. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h5)

question: How does placing a pit latrine too close to a food preparation area threaten health?

options.A: Smoke from cooking will fill up the latrine pit
options.B: Groundwater will turn the food completely bitter
options.C: Flies can carry pathogens from the latrine to the food
options.D: The smell will ruin the appetite of the consumers

explanation: Insects act as mechanical vectors, transferring filth and pathogens directly from human waste to uncovered food. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h5)

question: What is the best approach when teaching food hygiene to local market vendors?

options.A: Issuing heavy fines without any prior explanation
options.B: Insisting they change their traditional recipes completely
options.C: Using local languages and practical, respectful demonstrations
options.D: Handing out lengthy English academic research papers

explanation: Adult learners respond best to respectful communication in familiar languages using practical demonstrations they can apply immediately. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h6)

question: Which community setting provides a strategic opportunity for nurses to educate mothers on food safety?
explanation: Mothers frequently visit immunization and antenatal clinics, making them an ideal audience for infant feeding and food hygiene education. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h6)
